content.comment_body: Hi everyone, I've been testing the [product_name] app and found it quite useful overall. However, I noticed it's missing a key feature: manual switching of connected devices on and off. Usually, I add either soft switches or cursor keys in my program for overriding automatic control, allowing manual activation of equipment like pumps. When using [product_name] programming software, I see the option to set Parameter VM mapping for many function blocks—but not for soft switches or cursor keys. This means I can't enable manual control of pumps through the app. Are there any workarounds for this, or perhaps a trick to achieve manual control? <edit> I’ve solved it myself—turns out it’s simply a matter of programming a network input. :D Thanks, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user points out an issue with manual override functionality in the [product_name] app, specifically the inability to map soft switches or cursor keys for direct manual control of devices, like pumps. This affects common scenarios where manual intervention is needed from the app. The user discovers a solution by programming a network input, providing a workaround for this limitation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] app, coupled with its corresponding programming software, to provide direct manual override capabilities for devices through mapped soft switches or cursor keys.
